knowledge_checks.title: Revision Recall: purpose map
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly names the three primary aims of CS1 data analysis with distinct actuarial examples and one reproducibility element?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: CS1 distinguishes descriptive, inferential, and predictive aims. Reproducibility requires a concrete repeatable analysis path.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Describe the observed portfolio, infer a population quantity, and predict a future outcome, with versioned data and scripted analysis.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Listing tools instead of aims, collapsing the aims, or swapping their roles.

choices.label: Descriptive: summarise claim sizes in a portfolio year. Inferential: estimate mean claim severity for a population of similar risks. Predictive: forecast next year's claim count for pricing. Reproducibility needs something concrete such as versioned data and a scripted analysis path.
The three aims are plotting, computing means, and using software. Reproducibility means saving the final chart.
All three aims mean inspecting observed claims, so one sample summary covers description, population inference, and future prediction.
Descriptive analysis forecasts future claims, inferential analysis reports only the observed sample, and predictive analysis estimates a fixed population parameter.

knowledge_checks.title: Revision Checkpoint: EDA tool judgement
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Claim amounts are strongly right-skewed and contain several large observations. Which descriptive analysis is most defensible?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the best summary and visualisation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Robust summaries and a distributional plot reveal centre, spread, skewness, and possible outliers without assuming errors.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Use the median, IQR, and a histogram or boxplot, then investigate the large claims.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using a mean-only summary or an unsuitable pie chart for skewed continuous data.

choices.label: Report the median and interquartile range, use a histogram or boxplot to show skew and extremes, and investigate large claims rather than deleting them automatically.
Report only the mean because it is the standard summary for every numerical variable.
Use a pie chart because it displays the shape of continuous claim amounts more clearly than a histogram.
Delete all claims above the upper quartile before calculating any summary.

knowledge_checks.title: Revision Checkpoint: association limits
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Two continuous variables have outliers and a strong monotone but nonlinear relationship. Which conclusion is justified?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Rank correlations measure monotone association without requiring linearity. Association alone does not establish causation.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Use Spearman's rho or Kendall's tau and avoid a causal claim.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using Pearson automatically or interpreting rank association as causation.

choices.label: Spearman's rank correlation or Kendall's tau can measure the monotone association and reduce sensitivity to extreme magnitudes, but neither establishes causation.
Pearson correlation must equal 1 because every monotone relationship is perfectly linear.
Kendall's tau proves that changing one variable causes the other to change.
No correlation measure can describe a nonlinear monotone relationship.
